Tachbrook Nursery School
“Children are exceptionally well cared for in this inclusive setting, where everyone iswelcomed and given a chance to succeed.”
Take a look at the full report below to learn more about what our nursery could offer your child.
Welcome
Dear all,
As Head of school at Tachbrook Nursery School, I am thrilled to extend a warm welcome to you and your family. Our school is a state-maintained setting dedicated to providing a high-quality, inclusive early education for children aged 2.6 to 4 years old. We offer a nurturing and engaging environment where every child can grow, learn, and thrive.
Josephine Baker
Community Feedback
“All staff members are welcoming and friendly, Tachbrook is a fantastic nursery.”
“All staff members are kind and compassionate.”
“Love my child’s progress book and seeing all that he has done.”
“We are very happy with everything, we couldn’t ask for a better nursery.”
“I think the staff is fantastic and love the approach of lot of communication being face to face and regular emails.”
“You have wonderful teachers- the best! We are so lucky.”
“I find every single one of them friendly and approachable.”
“You’re doing a great job, keep it up.”
“We think Tachbrook is a wonderful place to learn. We feel very lucky that our child has been able to learn and grow here.”
“I have seen my child very well cared for when sick or upset.”
Our Values
We asked our educators, parents and students what they think our values are as a school. As a result we have these three words that represent us, and our community.
Happy, Healthy and High Expectations
Children love coming to school, and are excited by engaging activities both indoors and outdoors. They thrive in our nurturing environment with exceptional care for them and their families. Together, we create a space where every child can grow, learn, and succeed.

Welcome
Dear all,
Welcome to Tachbrook Nursery School!
As Head of school at Tachbrook Nursery School, I am thrilled to extend a warm welcome to you and your family. Our school is a state-maintained setting dedicated to providing a high-quality, inclusive early education for children aged 2.6 to 4 years old. We offer a nurturing and engaging environment where every child can grow, learn, and thrive.
We offer a variety of flexible places to suit the needs of families, including 15-hour and 30-hour options. For those who require additional hours, subject to availability, we are also able to offer a limited number of fee-paying, full-time and part-time places. Please contact the school directly for more information.
Our term-time education is organised as follows:
To ensure a smooth start and end to each session, we kindly ask that you arrive on time as the door remains open for 15 minutes at the beginning and end of each session.
At Tachbrook, we are committed to providing a safe, stimulating, and fun learning experience for all our children. Our experienced and caring staff are dedicated to supporting every child’s development in a positive and welcoming atmosphere.
Thank you for considering Tachbrook Nursery School. We look forward to meeting you and working together to support your child’s educational journey. Please feel free to explore our website for more information.
Warm regards,Josephine BakerHead of School

Information for Parents and Carers
At a glance
Term dates 2026/2027
Tachbrook Nursery School — Connected Futures Partnership
Download the school calendar (Word)
INSET days: 7 September 2026; 4 January 2027; 5 January 2027; 7 June 2027; 22 July 2027. School is closed to pupils on these days.
Initial visits: 2, 3 and 4 September 2026 — marked as open to staff only in the school calendar.
Term dates 2027/2028
Tachbrook Nursery School — Connected Futures Partnership
Download the school calendar (PDF)
INSET days: 1 September 2027; 2 September 2027; 3 January 2028; 4 January 2028; 5 June 2028. School is closed to pupils on these days.
Other shaded closures: 3 and 6 September 2027.
Absences
If you want someone else to collect your child, you must tell us beforehand. We will not let a child leave school with someone we do not know.
If your child is too unwell to come to school, please phone us before 9.00 – 0207 186 0081.
Term dates
View the 2027/28 calendar on this page
Download 2026/27 (Word) Download 2027/28 (PDF)
Uniform
We play outside throughout the year whatever the weather. We provide appropriate clothing for the children to wear in all weathers.
School meals
You may be eligible for Free School Meals and are advised to apply.
Click here for the link to apply for Free School Meals.
Children can help themselves to fruit, milk and water throughout the nursery session.
The nursery is a nut free zone. Please help us to keep all the children safe by not allowing your child to bring sweets, crisps or other food into the nursery.
Payments
All 3-4 year olds are entitled to a free 15 hour nursery place. Working families may be eligible for a 30 hour free nursery place.
Please check your eligibility for the 30 hour code.
15 hours of free child-care for 2 year olds is available through 2 options.
Additional payments can be made for extra nursery sessions (depending on availability of places). Please contact the office for further information.
Safeguarding
Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility. Our governing body and staff work to protect children from harm, promote their welfare and identify concerns early.
Our safeguarding contacts are:
If you have a concern, speak to a member of staff immediately or call 020 7186 0081.
Read our current safeguarding and child protection policy in the Connected Futures Partnership policy library.
Josie Baker — Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL)
Rebecca Tuttle — Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
Medical
It is very important that we are kept informed about any health conditions, including allergies, and that you share medical advice with us. Please also keep us updated of any changes which may affect your child’s social, emotional and psychological well-being.
If your child has an accident or becomes unwell at nursery we will inform you.
Behaviour
Learning to behave appropriately in a group is a very important part of nursery education. Most children will sometimes find it hard to take turns and share; some children might take a while to learn how to solve disagreements through talk rather than hitting someone.
We help them to learn acceptable ways of expressing emotions and needs by:
You may have different methods at home but we ask you to support what we do at school because we have to consider the care and development of all the children here.
Talking about each other’s feelings
Further reading
Settling In
general information and home to school links
Paper Copies, Security, Registration, Punctuality and Attendance, Illness and Accidents at School, Clothing, Sweets, Toys, and Birthdays, Mobile Phones
Borrowing Books, Library Friday, Outings, Parties, Behaviour and Discipline
learning and teaching
Young children learn in a variety of ways: through experimenting, watching, practising, listening, talking, playing. They learn in a variety of social situations: alone, in pairs, in larger groups. Above all, they learn at their own pace, building on knowledge, understanding, skills and attitudes already developed.
Free School Meals
Providing children with nutritious meals during the school day is vital for their health and wellbeing, and the council’s new online system makes applying for Free School Meals quicker and easier than ever.
Moving on to primary
Lunch
At Tachbrook all children who attend full-time eat lunch whilst at school. Children can either bring a packed lunch from home or choose to have a hot meal. They sit in ‘family style’ small groups of about 6-8 children and a meal supervisor. The meal supervisor will help your child eat their lunch and encourage your child to try and taste foods provided.

Our Curriculum
Learning through play, indoors and outdoors
Children explore a wide range of activities and experiences in our classrooms and large garden throughout the year. Our curriculum supports their development and builds a strong foundation for primary school.
We follow the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS), which continues through Reception. Our values — Happy, Healthy and High Expectations — guide the way we help children learn and thrive.
A carefully planned curriculum
Our Curriculum Progression Map sets out small steps in learning across the nursery year. Topics are linked to fiction and non-fiction books, with planned opportunities to develop knowledge, understanding, skills and positive attitudes.
Each half-term overview brings together key questions, vocabulary, books, songs and rhymes, circle time and focused activities. Staff guide children through playful learning, helping them build on what they already know.
The seven areas of learning
Working with families
Speak to your child’s key person about this half-term’s learning and how you can support it at home. Paper copies of our curriculum policies are available from the office.
View or download our curriculum policy · Explore our curriculum policies

A warm welcome to our inclusive community.
We believe that identifying and supporting children with SEND is not about labelling children, it is about giving some extra time to observe, discuss and support the children who need it. First and foremost, the child is an individual with special interests, skills and talents.
Please don’t hesitate to talk to us if you have any concerns or would like advice. You can speak to your child’s key worker, to Laura McMullan, our SENCO and ARP Lead Teacher, or to Josie Baker, Head of School. To arrange a conversation, call 020 7186 0081 or email office@tachbrooknursery.co.uk.
We look forward to speaking to you and working together to provide the very best start for your child.
Our SEND policy
Read the approved CFP SEND policy online · Download the SEND policy

Joining Our Nursery
Join Us
If you would like your child to attend our school, please see full details of our admission arrangements below.
HOW TO APPLYYou can put your child’s name on the application list when they are 18 months old. Please ring/ email the school to book a place on one of our monthly tours, if you like what you have seen, you can collect an application form.
We offer places from 2.6 to 4 years old. Three year old’s are eligible for a 15 or 30 hour place the term after their third Birthday. Two year old’s are eligible for a 15 hour place the term after their second Birthday. Due to the challenging nature of our nursery learning environment and garden two year old’s will be offered a place at the Headteacher’s discretion once the child is two and a half years old. For more information please see our Admissions policy.
If there are not enough places for all the children who would like to attend we allocate places in this order:
1. Looked After Children2. Children with exceptional medical or social need for a place at this school3. Children with brothers or sisters already attending4. Children for whom this is the nearest community school5. Children who live nearest to the school
Tours for New Parents
Tours last approximately 45 minutes. Please email or phone the school to book a place on the tour. The Head of school will answer any questions you have after the tour and give you an application form should you wish to apply for a place at Tachbrook nursery school.
Wednesday 14th October 9.45am
Thursday 26th November 9.45am
30 HOUR PLACES FOR 3 YEAR OLDS (Full time: Monday-Friday 9.00-3.45)
To qualify for a 30 hour full time place you will need to check your eligibility here or see ‘Will I Qualify for 30 hours free childcare’ form below. When you have received your 30 hour eligibility code you will need to give this code to the school.
15 HOUR PLACES FOR 3 YEAR OLDS
All 3 and 4 year olds are entitled to 15 hours of free childcare. We offer the 15 hours per week, either five mornings or five afternoons.
Morning places 9:00- 12:00pm Afternoon places 12:45 -3:45pm
15 HOUR PLACES FOR 2 YEAR OLDS
We offer 2 year old places for children from 2.6 years old, 15 hours a week, either five mornings or five afternoons a week. Due to the challenging nature of the nursery environment and garden the nursery may not be suitable for all 2.6 year old’s and places are offered at the Headteacher’s discretion.
To qualify for a 15 hour two year old place you will need to check your eligibility here. If you are eligible you can apply using the ‘Parent Portal’ link here.
If your child is not eligible you can pay for a place. Please see ‘Paid for Places’ information (below).
Morning places 9.00-12.00pmAfternoon places 12.45-3.45pm
For all Government 15 and 30 hour places your child will be entitled to a place the term after they are 2/3 years old

PAID FOR PLACES (15 & 30 hours)
We have a number of paid for places for children from 2.6 years old. We also have a small number of paid for places for 3 year old children who may not qualify for the 30 hour free government place.
Please read documents below for more information.

If you’d like us to call you regarding a nursery tour or joining our school, please submit your email and phone number via this form and we will ensure you get a response from our team within 1-3 business days.
